names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 3 mai, «Sfânta Muceniță Mavra».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 3 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Τιμόθεος και Μαύρα», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 3. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученици Тимотије и Мавра.“ Свети мученици heads both and belongs to neither name alone — мученици is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types` and `honorific.js` composes back — so stripping it leaves the bare forename. The kinship clause this corpus keeps in the English display name is the body's, and the village the other two calendars name is on no part of this page. The form meets no other folder in any language, which was measured rather than assumed.
Read out of the calendar’s name link for 3 мая ст. ст., which gives «Мавра Фиваидская, мц.»; the rank word is not part of the stored form. The day line itself declines her as «Мавры» alone.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 3 мая ст. ст. — «Мчч. Тимофея и Мавры (ок. 286).»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 3 mai — «Sfânta Muceniță Mavra»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 3ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Τιμόθεος και Μαύρα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 3 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps her, and it is plainly the same woman: of Panapea in the Thebaid, married twenty days when her husband was denounced, tortured and crucified with him. It prints **no year**, so `dates` stays absent. **The Greek is much fuller about her than about him** — the hair torn out, the fingers cut off, the cauldron of boiling water that did not scald her, the prefect's hand dissolved by the water she threw on it from her own palm, the devil's cup of milk and honey and then the river of milk and honey, both refused with «Δεν πρόκειται να πιώ απ' αυτά. Θα πιώ από το ουράνιο ποτήρι που μου πρόσφερε ο Χριστός», and the angel who showed her a throne, a white robe and a crown, and then a higher throne and robe and crown for her husband, «Η διαφορά του τόπου δηλώνει το γεγονός ότι ο άντρας σου υπήρξε η αιτία της σωτηρίας σου»; and the nine days the two of them hung on the cross. **It adds her relics and her patronage**: «Η Κάρα της Αγίας βρίσκεται στον ομώνυμο Ναό Κοιλανίου Λεμεσού Κύπρου», with fragments at Kykkos in Cyprus and at the church of Saint George of the Greeks in Venice, and «Πολιούχος: Λευκάδα (Πόλη) (Αγία Μαύρα), Ρουπάκι Ηλείας». It tells at length how her veneration reached Lefkada, which was itself called Αγία Μαύρα: the Angevin lords who took the island in 1331 came from a town of Sainte Maure in France and named the island after it and built a Latin chapel, and in the mid-fifteenth century Helen Palaiologina, daughter of Thomas Palaiologos and wife of the despot Lazar Vuković, vowed a church to her in a storm on the way to her daughter's wedding to Duke Leonardo III Tocco, and built it. **Those are dedications and not relations**, and none of the persons in that account has a folder. Two apolytikia and one kontakion of the page's eight hymns are the joint service of the pair and are stored on both folders; the rest were left.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 16.05.2026 (3. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Тимотије и Мавра.“

attestations.note: **The heading enumerates both — „Свети мученици Тимотије и Мавра.“ — so the citation above is that heading whole**, per BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4 and the coordinator's ruling, and both names are folders this corpus already keeps. The day is Julian 3 May, the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek keep them on. The identification is not in doubt: a reader of the church and the bride he had been married twenty days, before Arian governor of the Thebaid under Diocletian, his ears pierced with iron and his eyes lost by it, her hair torn out and her fingers cut off, and the two crucified together. **A first date for both folders**: „Чесно пострадаше за Христа 286. године“, where doxologia's account breaks off before either death and saint.gr gives no year at all. New besides, and this is the only one of the three accounts that reaches the end: that they were crucified **facing each other**, „једно према другом“; that they hung alive **nine full days, counselling and encouraging one another**, and gave up their spirits **on the tenth**, where saint.gr has nine days pass and no tenth; and Timothy's answer about the instruments of torture, „И ти не видиш ангеле Божје који ме крепе“, which is a different exchange from doxologia's about the books and the angels. This page has **nothing** of doxologia's cauldron, its coals, its scalded governor or the father Picolpos, and nothing of the books. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nestricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Timotei și Mavra», Glasul 4

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their struggles have won from Thee, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Thy strength, they overthrew their tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ὡς ζεῦγος ὁμόζυγον, καὶ ξυνωρὶς θαυμαστή, Τιμόθεε πάνσοφε, καὶ Μαῦρα νύμφη Χριστοῦ, ἐνθέως ἠθλήσατε, σύμμορφοι γὰρ ὀφθέντες, τῶν παθῶν τοῦ Κυρίου, δόξης ἀκατάλυτου, ἠξιώθητε ἄμφω, πρεσβεύοντες τῷ Σωτήρι, ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ἠμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε, on the page of «Άγιοι Τιμόθεος και Μαύρα» — the joint apolytikion of the pair, which names both

english.text: As a yoked pair and a wondrous couple, all-wise Timothy and Maura the bride of Christ, ye contended divinely; for being made conformable to the sufferings of the Lord, ye were both counted worthy of indissoluble glory, interceding with the Saviour for our souls.

hymns.text: Τοὺς πολυτρόπους αἰκισμοὺς ἐνεγκόντες, καὶ τοὺς στεφάνους ἐκ Θεοῦ εἰληφότες, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πρεσβεύσατε πρὸς Κύριον, μνήμην τὴν πανίερον, τὴν ὑμῶν ἐκτελούντων, μέγιστε Τιμόθεε, καὶ ἀοίδιμε Μαύρα, τοῦ εἰρηνεῦσαι πόλιν καὶ λαόν· αὐτός ἐστι γάρ, πιστῶν τὸ κραταίωμα.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ', Ὁ ὑψωθεὶς ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ, on the page of «Άγιοι Τιμόθεος και Μαύρα» — the joint kontakion of the pair, which names both

english.text: Having borne torments of every kind and received your crowns from God, intercede with the Lord for us who keep your all-holy memory, O greatest Timothy and renowned Maura, that city and people may have peace; for He is the strength of the faithful.

hymns.text: Мученицы Твои, Господи,/ во страданиих своих венцы прияша нетленныя от Тебе, Бога нашего,/ имуще бо крепость Твою,/ мучителей низложиша,/ сокрушиша и демонов немощныя дерзости./ Тех молитвами/ спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 3 мая ст. ст., «Тропарь мучеников Тимофея чтеца и Мавры», глас 4 — the common of martyrs, printed under their names and therefore theirs

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, received from thee, our God, incorruptible crowns in their sufferings; for having thy strength they threw down their tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. By their prayers save our souls.

hymns.text: Многообразныя язвы претерпевше/ и венцы от Бога приемше,/ о нас молитеся ко Господу,/ память всесвященную вашу совершающих,/ превеликий Тимофее и преславная Мавро,/ еже умирити град и люди,/ Той бо есть верных утверждение.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 3 мая ст. ст., «Кондак мучеников Тимофея чтеца и Мавры», глас 4

english.text: Having endured wounds of many kinds and received crowns from God, pray to the Lord for us who keep your all-sacred memory, O most great Timothy and most glorious Maura, that he would give peace to the city and to the people; for he is the strengthening of the faithful.

death.note: The Охридски пролог for 3. мај ст. ст. closes the entry „Чесно пострадаше за Христа 286. године.“ — **the first year any calendar read for this folder has given**. doxologia's account breaks off before either death and prints no year at all; saint.gr's notice ends with the nine days on the cross and says expressly nothing of a year. The Prologue's own setting agrees with both: Arian governor of the Thebaid in the time of the emperor Diocletian, whose reign began in 284, so 286 contradicts nothing either page prints. `node .tmp/dd.mjs "286"` reads it in both packs.
